facts: A16 keeps CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION at 6 and does not rewrite the A05 migration engine.
Recovery CLI owns the profile flock through an A16-only guard that does not bind the graphical activation socket.
A16 snapshots are created with the SQLite/rusqlite Online Backup API and are bound to manifests containing hash, size, schema/app version, integrity/FK result and selected row counts.
Normal startup runs a read-only recovery preflight before writable repository open and creates a verified A16 snapshot before migrating an older supported schema.
Confirmed restore verifies the selected point, preserves a healthy pre-restore point when possible, quarantines current DB/WAL/SHM/journal, installs the snapshot and post-verifies integrity/hash.
Safe logical export excludes operational/session/capability state and is explicitly distinct from p2p_planner_bundle.
Recovery preflight validates the migration-ledger prefix and profile_meta schema version for older supported schemas before allowing a writable migration.
Quarantine preparation rolls already-moved profile files back if required directory durability sync fails before snapshot installation.
inferences: Because the CLI recovery path returns before graphical/runtime composition, it should remain usable when WebView construction itself fails, provided the executable and its dynamic dependencies can enter main.
Retaining all verified A16 restore points without pruning satisfies the minimum last-good retention requirement until a future retention policy is introduced.
proposals: Use the canonical A16 UTS Rust tests and real-binary host probe as the acceptance gate before calling A16 host-verified.
Keep damaged-SQLite best-effort salvage and any future recovery GUI separate from the fail-closed A16 core.
unresolved: Cargo/rustc/rustfmt are unavailable in the patch-construction environment, so Rust compilation and the real-binary probe are not claimed here.
The A16 recovery logical export is a salvage artifact and has no direct import contract.
A loader failure before main cannot be repaired by the application without violating the package-manager privilege boundary.
